title: Cloudflare Migrates JavaScript CDN Serving 9B Requests a Day to Its Developer Platform
gist: Cloudflare moved cdnjs — an open source JS/CSS CDN serving ~9 billion requests a day and used by roughly 12% of websites — entirely off a mixed Cloudflare/Google Cloud Platform publishing stack onto its own Developer Platform (Workers, R2, Workflows, Queues, Durable Objects, KV, Containers), making R2 the source of truth. The migration is an explicit dogfooding exercise that forced Cloudflare to raise platform limits by orders of magnitude and revealed where Workers still cannot do the job.

themes.theme: Displacing Google Cloud from the publishing path

insights.claim: Cloudflare has migrated cdnjs entirely onto its own Developer Platform, replacing publishing infrastructure that had been split across Cloudflare and Google Cloud Platform with Workers, R2, Workflows, Queues, Durable Objects, KV and Containers.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: A concrete instance of Cloudflare's developer platform displacing hyperscaler primitives for a real production workload — the substitution risk GCP faces at the edge-adjacent layer.

insights.claim: The legacy cdnjs publishing path depended on 26 Google Cloud Functions divided into alphabetic shards to poll npm for package updates, Google Cloud Storage for packages, Pub/Sub for messaging, and a virtual machine running git-sync for repository content.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Shows the specific GCP line items retired in the swap; alphabetic sharding of 26 functions is a marker of the workaround-heavy architecture that newer workflow primitives eliminate.
insights.locator: The publishing path, however, remained distributed

insights.claim: The cdnjs GitHub repository had grown beyond 1.1 TB of packed storage with published files duplicated across both GitHub and KV, an unsustainable state that motivated making R2 the single source of truth.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Git-as-artifact-store breaks down at terabyte scale; object storage as source of truth is the pattern to expect across package ecosystems.
insights.locator: At the same time, the GitHub repository had grown beyond 1.1 TB

insights.claim: cdnjs serves approximately 9 billion requests per day, averaging 108,000 requests per second across more than 330 Cloudflare data centers, with a 98.6% cache hit rate.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Hard throughput benchmark for what a Workers/R2 stack sustains in production — useful for sizing claims by competing edge platforms.
insights.quote: cdnjs now serves approximately 9 billion requests per day, averaging 108,000 requests per second across more than 330 Cloudflare data centers

insights.claim: cdnjs is used by approximately 12% of websites, making a single Cloudflare-operated open source CDN a systemic dependency of the public web.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Concentration risk and strategic leverage in one number — an outage or supply-chain compromise here has web-wide blast radius, and it locks a large audience into Cloudflare's edge.
insights.locator: The service reports a 98.6% cache hit rate

insights.claim: Cloudflare positions the cdnjs migration explicitly as dogfooding its Developer Platform at the scale of a widely used public service, using the project as a credibility proof point rather than only an internal cleanup.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Marketing intent is the tell: Cloudflare is selling Workers/R2/Workflows as an enterprise-grade alternative to hyperscaler serverless, and this is the reference story.
insights.quote: Cloudflare described the migration as an example of dogfooding its Developer Platform at the scale of a widely used public service.
insights.locator: Cloudflare described the migration as an example of dogfooding

insights.claim: The new cdnjs architecture assigns R2 the artifacts, KV the package metadata, versions and SRI hashes, a Worker the request handling, Workers Cache the caching layer, and Cloudflare Workflows the publishing orchestration.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: A reference decomposition for building a package CDN on edge primitives — the template competing platforms will be measured against.
insights.quote: The resulting architecture uses R2 for artifacts, KV for metadata, Workers for delivery, and Workflows for publishing.
insights.locator: The resulting architecture uses R2 for artifacts

insights.claim: Cloudflare mirrors published cdnjs content to DigitalOcean Spaces as a fallback in case R2 cannot serve a file, keeping a competitor's object storage in the critical path even after consolidating onto its own platform.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Even the vendor dogfooding its own storage will not single-source it — a quiet admission that multi-provider redundancy remains necessary at this criticality tier.
insights.quote: Published content is additionally mirrored to DigitalOcean Spaces as a fallback if R2 cannot serve a file.
insights.locator: The new architecture makes Cloudflare R2 the source of truth

insights.claim: cdnjs package ingestion runs as a scheduled Cloudflare Workflow that checks npm and GitHub for releases, downloads into R2 and spawns per-file processing workflows that extract, minify, compress, store, update KV metadata and refresh the Algolia search index, with workflow state allowing resumption from the last completed step after a failure.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Durable-execution workflows replacing cron-plus-queue glue is the emerging serverless pattern; Algolia's presence shows search remains an outsourced component even in a fully dogfooded stack.
insights.locator: Package ingestion is now orchestrated through Cloudflare Workflows

insights.claim: Preserving exact package bytes was a hard constraint in the migration because any change to minification or compression would alter Subresource Integrity hashes and break consuming sites.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: SRI turns a CDN's build pipeline into an immutable contract — a real constraint on how quickly any package CDN can modernize its tooling.
insights.quote: Preserving package bytes was critical because changes to minification or compression could alter SRI hashes.

insights.claim: Cloudflare had to run cdnjs compression in Containers rather than Workers because the existing compression algorithms require buffering an entire library in memory, a workload Workers cannot handle today.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Concrete boundary of the Workers execution model — memory-bound batch work still needs containers, which is why Cloudflare shipped Containers at all.
insights.quote: Compression presented a constraint because the existing processing algorithms require an entire library to be buffered in memory.

insights.claim: Cloudflare says it is exploring streaming support that could eventually move memory-bound compression processing from Containers back into Workers, signaling a roadmap direction for narrowing the Workers capability gap.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: If streaming lands, Containers becomes a transitional product rather than a permanent tier — watch for it as a margin and simplicity lever.
insights.locator: Cloudflare said it is exploring streaming support

insights.claim: The migration forced Cloudflare to raise its own platform ceilings dramatically — Worker subrequests from 1,000 to 10 million, and Workflow steps from 1,024 to 10,000 with up to 25,000 configurable — showing the prior limits were far below real production needs.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: A 10,000x subrequest increase is a signal that published serverless limits are soft and that dogfooding is what actually surfaces them — evaluate competing platforms' limits skeptically.
insights.quote: prompting Cloudflare to raise Worker subrequests from 1,000 to 10 million and Workflow steps from 1,024 to 10,000, with up to 25,000 configurable
insights.locator: The migration also exposed platform limits

insights.claim: The 2026 migration builds on a 2020 change that already moved cdnjs file serving to Workers and Workers KV — replacing dedicated origin machines for normal traffic while keeping an external origin fallback, and adding precompressed Brotli and gzip assets — meaning the serving layer moved six years before the publishing layer.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: The six-year gap between migrating reads and migrating writes is a realistic timeline for how slowly stateful publishing paths move, even inside the vendor.
insights.locator: The migration builds on a 2020 architectural change
